title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Discover the functional study nooks, collaborative labs, and quiet retreats that define daily life for Babson students beyond the standard admissions highlights.

cards.title: Global Lounge
cards.subtitle: Reynolds Campus Center
cards.notes: Visit this 'campus living room' to study on comfortable furniture or borrow outdoor lawn games and board games between classes.
cards.short_summary: A central social and study hub in the Reynolds Campus Center featuring flexible seating and game rentals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Global Lounge in Reynolds Campus Center is described as a 'campus living room' where students can hang out, study, and borrow lawn or board games.
cards.access_notes: Open daily during Reynolds Campus Center operating hours; accessible via student OneCard.

cards.title: Weissman Foundry
cards.subtitle: Collaborative Maker Space
cards.notes: Access the woodshop, digital fabrication studio, or social kitchen to prototype products and collaborate with Olin and Wellesley students.
cards.short_summary: A cross-campus maker space for Babson, Olin, and Wellesley students to create and prototype ideas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Weissman Foundry is a collaborative space featuring a woodshop, digital fabrication studio, and social kitchen for student prototyping.
cards.access_notes: Open to students from Babson, Olin, and Wellesley; specific workshop hours apply for equipment use.

cards.title: Horn Library Quiet Nooks
cards.subtitle: Quiet Study Areas
cards.notes: Find a quiet carrel in the renovated library wings for focused individual work away from the busier collaborative commons.
cards.short_summary: Dedicated quiet study areas and carrels within the renovated Horn Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Horn Library offers quiet study nooks and carrels designed for individual focus following its recent renovations.
cards.access_notes: Quiet zones are strictly enforced; check library website for current semester hours.

cards.title: Graduate Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: Olin Hall Ground Floor
cards.notes: Relax or watch TV in this ground-floor lounge, which serves as the primary social hub for the graduate student community.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated lounge for graduate students located on the ground floor of Olin Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Graduate Student Lounge on the ground floor of Olin Hall is a place for graduate students to relax and watch TV.
cards.access_notes: Primarily for graduate student use; accessible during Olin Hall building hours.

cards.title: Glavin Family Chapel
cards.subtitle: Nondenominational Sanctuary
cards.notes: Step into this glass-walled sanctuary for a moment of quiet meditation or to attend diverse spiritual services.
cards.short_summary: A peaceful, nondenominational chapel featuring glass walls that look out onto the campus woods.
cards.evidence_claim: The Glavin Family Chapel is a 150-seat nondenominational sanctuary used for meditation and religious services.
cards.access_notes: Open for quiet reflection when services are not in progress.

cards.title: Babson Ceramics Studio
cards.subtitle: Sorenson Visual Arts Center
cards.notes: Join as a member to access pottery wheels and kilns; the studio is located within the Sorenson Visual Arts Center in Trim Hall.
cards.short_summary: A fully equipped ceramics studio available to the Babson community for a semester fee.
cards.evidence_claim: The Babson Ceramics Studio is located in the Sorenson Visual Arts Center within Trim Hall and offers memberships to students.
cards.access_notes: Accessible 8 a.m.–10 p.m. daily via OneCard for registered members.

cards.title: Park Manor Central Basement
cards.subtitle: Creative & Study Rooms
cards.notes: Utilize the music practice room, dance studio, and quiet study areas tucked away in the basement of this residence hall.
cards.short_summary: A multi-use basement space in Park Manor Central featuring music and dance facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Park Manor Central's basement includes study rooms, a music room, and a dance studio for student use.
cards.access_notes: Building access restricted to residents; facilities may be bookable for other students.

cards.title: The Horizon Room
cards.subtitle: Trim Dining Hall Extension
cards.notes: Head to this 200-seat extension of the main dining hall for a slightly quieter meal or group meeting during peak hours.
cards.short_summary: A large seating extension of the Trim Dining Hall used for meals and student gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Horizon Room is an extension of the Trim dining area providing an additional 200 seats for students.
cards.source_title: Babson College Trim Dining Hall | Gilbane Building Company
cards.access_notes: Open during Trim Dining Hall meal service hours.

cards.title: Kerry Murphy Healey Park
cards.subtitle: Centennial Park
cards.notes: Relax in the Adirondack chairs surrounding the iconic Babson World Globe in this park established for the college's centennial.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped park featuring the historic Babson World Globe and outdoor seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Kerry Murphy Healey Park is home to the Babson World Globe and offers a space for students to sit and enjoy the outdoors.
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor park; globe rotation is scheduled periodically.

cards.title: International Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Reynolds Campus Center
cards.notes: Find a quiet spot to read or study in this dedicated room located within the bustling campus center.
cards.short_summary: A quiet reading and study room located inside the Reynolds Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Reynolds Campus Center contains an international reading room as a dedicated space for students.
cards.source_title: Babson College | Reynolds Campus Center | William Rawn Associates Architects
cards.access_notes: Open during Reynolds Campus Center hours; intended for quiet study.
